forest-depths.$description: Forest Depths — Dark elevated surface for cards, headers, and contained panels. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

moss-shadow.$description: Moss Shadow — Gray action color for filled buttons, selected navigation states, and focused conversion moments.

lichen-sage.$description: Lichen Sage — Secondary muted text, link underline on dark, and badge border color — sits between Moss Shadow and Pure White as the off-tone voice

pale-fern.$description: Pale Fern — Medium-contrast borders, control outlines, and structural separators.

electric-sprout.$description: Electric Sprout — Green action color for filled buttons, selected navigation states, and focused conversion moments.

deep-verdant.$description: Deep Verdant — Secondary accent for link borders, icon strokes, and hover-active states — a quieter green that supports Sprout without competing

sprout-wash.$description: Sprout Wash — Light green badge background and success-tint surface — the diluted form of Electric Sprout for soft status chips

mist-green.$description: Mist Green — Light sage link border and chip outline on bone surfaces — a low-contrast divider that reads as green without demanding attention

onyx-olive.$description: Onyx Olive — Primary achromatic dark — body copy on white, borders on light cards, and the dominant hairline color across the whole system

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Light-section page background, text on dark surfaces, and inverted badge fills — the greenhouse bench

bone-white.$description: Bone White — Card surface on light sections — warm off-white that prevents the page from reading sterile, never pure #fff when elevated

soft-mist.$description: Soft Mist — Cool-tinted heading rule and quiet secondary border — the only neutral that isn't green-tinted

cool-stone.$description: Cool Stone — Muted UI surface for disabled controls, low-emphasis panels, and placeholder blocks.

carbon.$description: Carbon — Link text and border on light surfaces — darker than Onyx Olive, used only where the link must read as a typographic accent rather than a button

ozik.$description: Hero and section display only — used for two or three words maximum per line. The ultra-tight 0.86 line-height stacks letterforms like glasshouse beams; the heavy weight on a near-black canvas is the system's signature.

aeonik.$description: Workhorse for every UI surface — nav, body, buttons, cards, inputs, headings up to 40px. 400 for body and labels, 500 for sub-labels, 600 for sub-headings, 700 for section titles and button labels. The negative letter-spacing tightens as size grows, giving headlines a compressed, technical feel without becoming a display face.

instrument-serif.$description: Editorial accent only — drops into badges, small pull quotes, and the occasional 32px sub-heading to break Aeonik's geometric monotony. The serif's organic stroke and slight +0.063em tracking at small sizes are the only warmth this system permits.
